title: PM vs Project Manager vs Designer: The Real Difference
description:
Product Manager, Project Manager, and Designer get confused constantly — even by the companies hiring for them. Here's the one-line distinction for each role: who owns the what, the when, and the how it feels. Straight from the Product Management Mastery Path.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/01-what-is-product-management/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Product Manager, Project Manager, Designer — even the companies hiring for them mix these up. Here's the actual line between them.
The Product Manager owns the what and why. Should we build this, and why does it matter? That's the PM's call.

display.heading: Product Manager
display.subheading: Owns the what and why -- "Should we build this, and why does it matter?"

beats.narration: The Project Manager owns the when and how it's coordinated. Is this on track, and what's blocking it?

display.heading: Project Manager
display.subheading: Owns the when -- "Is this on track, and what's blocking it?"

beats.narration: And the designer owns how it feels and works — the best experience for solving the problem, built closely with the PM.

display.heading: Designer
display.subheading: Owns how it feels -- "What's the best experience for solving this?"

beats.narration: Simple shorthand: whether to build it is a PM call. When it ships is project management. How it feels is design. Startups without a dedicated project manager just make PMs absorb that work — it doesn't redefine the role.

display.heading: The shorthand
display.subheading: Whether = PM. When = Project Manager. How it feels = Design.
